items.title: Joe Ascione interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: Mike Mainieri, first record. Selden Powell, Earl May, McKenna.

ctx.x: In some of your promo material I read it says you’re a protégé of Buddy Rich. Is that something that you would consider or is that something that people write, for something to write?

Here’s the true story. When I was a young boy Gene Krupa was my idol. I met him in 1971 when I was ten and then he died in ’73 and I was really sad, and then I heard Buddy Rich, one of my male cousins who played drums gave me a record, a 1959 recording, “The Driver” it was called. Mike Mainieri, first record. Selden Powell, Earl May, McKenna. And it was like what is this, two, three drummers? I couldn’t understand what was going on. My ear to the stereo. So he became my new guy. So then I got to hear him and meet…
I want to think about that one for a minute.
